advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] When the meter is degraded, do not trust a partial total below threshold to skip enforcement; force a CE read (or fail closed) so a dropped region cannot hide over-cap spend.
evidence: handler.py:549-556 old-style unavailable path forces `spend = THRESHOLD_USD` (fail-closed) when `metered is None`
handler.py:557-564 degraded branch uses `spend = metered.total` (the partial, under-reported total) with no fail-closed floor
handler.py:534 `near_threshold = metered_total is not None and metered_total * 5 >= THRESHOLD_USD * 4` — a partial that dropped a whole region can fall below 80% and skip the CE force-poll
handler.py:44-46 module contract: 'set deliberately HIGH so an unpriced model trips the cap early rather than slipping under it. Failing closed is the entire point of a cap.'
handler.py:621 `elif spend >= THRESHOLD_USD and not attached:` — attach depends entirely on the possibly-under-reported degraded `spend`
advisory.finding: A degraded partial meter (one region's CloudWatch failed but another contributed) uses the under-reported partial total for the attach decision, whereas the old code fell back to spend=THRESHOLD_USD on any regional ClientError. A failed region whose lost spend would exceed the cap can leave the partial total below THRESHOLD_USD and below the 80% near-threshold gate, so CE is not force-polled and the cap does not trip — hidden spend, contrary to the module's fail-closed design.
scenarios: A region raises ClientError on list_metrics/get_metric_data after another region already contributed; the failed region's spend was the bulk of the day's Bedrock cost; partial total < 80% threshold and CE not due → cap never trips despite real spend over cap.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat a degraded meter as a trigger to force (or at least not suppress) the authoritative CE read, since the partial total cannot certify 'not close'.
evidence: handler.py:534 near_threshold uses `metered_total` which for a degraded result is the partial sum only
handler.py:528-532 comment reasons about the fully-unavailable meter case, not the degraded-partial case
test_degraded_partial_meter_below_near_threshold_respects_ce_interval asserts CE is NOT polled (fake_aws.ce.calls == 0) for a degraded partial at 70% of threshold — codifying the gap
advisory.finding: When metered is degraded, the near-threshold CE force-poll gate is evaluated only on the partial total, so a degraded meter does NOT force an authoritative CE read even though a region's spend is missing. The code comment at lines 528-532 justifies not force-polling only for a fully-unavailable meter ('it cannot say we are close'); a degraded partial CAN be materially under 80% purely because a region is missing, yet the same skip applies.
scenarios: Two-region deployment, one region CloudWatch-down, partial=70% of cap, CE last polled <1h ago → CE skipped, degraded partial accepted as effective spend.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface metered.failures (regions) in the return payload and/or degraded notifications, or drop the unused failure detail.
evidence: handler.py:558 only `metered.degraded` is read; `metered.failures` is never referenced in handler()
handler.py:641-650 return dict has no field for failed regions
handler.py:287-291 MeteredSpend.failures is populated but unused downstream
advisory.finding: MeteredFailure carries region and exception_class detail, and the commit message says the result returns 'failed region details', but the handler consumes only the boolean `metered.degraded`; the per-region failure list is never surfaced in the return payload, notification bodies, or logs beyond the per-region error already logged in _record_metered_failure.
scenarios: Operator reading the Lambda return payload or a TRIPPED/WARNING notification cannot tell which region degraded without scraping raw CloudWatch logs.
